content.comment_body: Hello, I've searched Google, this forum, and the [company_name] website, but I'm still unclear about how the basic and expansion modules are compatible or interoperable. My current setup uses [article_no] (230V base module) and three [article_no] (230V relay modules). This works as expected. Now, I want to add a heater controller for a sauna. I ordered a PT100 to 0-10V converter to connect a temperature sensor to the analog input of the [article_no], since there's no room left on the DIN rail for a dedicated temperature input expansion module. However, I realized the base module doesn't have analog inputs, so I ordered a different base module [article_no] with analog inputs. I do have space for a separate power supply, since this module doesn't support 230V input. The problem is, the expansion relay modules don't physically fit—the plastic connectors don't match. Any advice?

You should have checked that before ordering. The 230V base modules have no analog inputs. The 12/24V versions have analog inputs but can't be used with 230V expansion modules due to a lack of electrical isolation between units—the mechanical coding prevents incorrect connections. Do not alter the coding to force compatibility. For your scenario, you can use: start with the 230V base module, add your three 230V expansion modules, and then include an analog input module such as AM2 or AM2 RTD. The analog modules provide electrical isolation on the input side. AM2 supports two 0-10V or 0/4-20mA inputs; AM2 RTD supports two PT100/1000 inputs.

Thank you, but I only have room for one base module (width 4) and three expansion modules (width 2), making the total width 10. Is there a way to fit this, or is it better to redesign the enclosure—which is a lot of work? There is space for the power supply, which doesn't need to be connected to the bus. I wish a bus cable existed so these modules could be installed across more than one DIN rail, but such an option doesn't seem available.
I am not familiar with your enclosure. Is it designed for just a single row, or does it support multiple rows?

You updated your previous post while I was replying. If you can place the power supply on a second row, then the 12/24V module can definitely fit. It’s possible to network this with your 230V module using Ethernet, allowing you to utilize the 0-10V transmitter in the 12/24V base and transfer temperature readings over the network to the 230V base.

I understand, but I prefer not to use two base modules—it would be too complicated. Thanks for your suggestions. It would be helpful to have a compatibility chart or matrix for the modules to understand the available options easily.
It’s always a good idea to ask in the forum before making purchases, rather than only after encountering problems.
Having spare parts isn't really an issue for me. I'm still searching for a comprehensive overview.
Could you clarify exactly what type of overview you are seeking?
Just a side note—are you aware of the [company_name] TIA Selection Tool? This tool helps you explore standard options for compatible products. You can access it via the cloud.
Yes, I’ve tried it, but initially it didn’t work. An update: it does work in Firefox, not in Chrome. I think I’ll be able to sort things out now, thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: Users frequently face challenges determining compatibility between base and expansion modules when mixing voltage types and integrating analog inputs. The lack of a clear compatibility guide results in wrong purchases and additional work. Physical and electrical safeguards, such as mechanical coding, are not strongly emphasized in planning materials, causing confusion during installation. Limited enclosure space further complicates system extension, increasing user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear, accessible compatibility charts to inform proper module selection based on voltage, input/output, and modular system design. They also wish for more flexible options, like modules that can be arranged across multiple DIN rails and straightforward solutions for integrating analog inputs without having to redesign enclosures.
